generator.what: quic-go 0.64.1 HTTP/3 client (docs/evidence/v07-h3-bench/load.go), real TLS verification against the fixture CA, no 0-RTT, no session resumption, closed-loop, no coordinated-omission correction

handshake.0_rtt: off (client does not attempt it; EQProxy does not implement it, ADR-0013)

disclosure.topology: one macOS host; Docker Desktop VM (10 vCPU, 8 GiB); origin, sink, both proxies and the generator are containers on one bridge network; no host port publishing on the measured path
equivalence: same HTTP/1.1 origin (1 KiB, Content-Length, keep-alive) and same body
same certificate, TLS 1.3, ALPN h3, cubic congestion control, 30 s idle timeout
same container port 19443; HAProxy uses a dedicated quic4@ bind for QUIC
no compression enabled in either product; no rules/rewrites in this scenario
no health checks in either product for this scenario (static origin)
differences: EQProxy translates every h3 request into one HTTP/1.1 exchange through its engine (architecture, ADR-0013); HAProxy forwards natively
HAProxy's TCP bind also offers h2/http1.1 (unused here); EQProxy's TCP path is part of the same listener

load_c8s8.note: Local HTTP/3 sink (quic-go server, same binary) measures the client+sink pair; the slower of the two is the ceiling, so this is a lower bound on what the generator can push.
